title: Existence of the unique isomorphism between orientation theories
as_he_states: For two theories satisfying the functorial, zero-dimensional and Stokes axioms, construct the isomorphism whose uniqueness the dimension induction proves.
plausible_today: There is exactly one isomorphism under the full displayed axioms. Its construction uses sign(det) actions, recursive reference orientations on R^n, and independence of adapted frames.
state_of_art: Exact written result in Hua2026 §57, unnumbered existence statement following Theorem57.2, pp284–285. The proof was read and rechecked; the cited Lean file was not compiled in this run. First circulation found November2026, no separate journal date verified.
why_open: The page’s induction establishes uniqueness but not existence. The missing construction is precisely the frame-independence step; no external source gives a historical reason for the unfinished proof.
worth: Worth an editorial proof and a targeted formal comparison, since the current public proof already settles the mathematical statement under the manuscript axioms.

title: Existence of an orientation theory
as_he_states: Construct at least one theory with the stated functor, Omega(0) normalization and natural half-space Stokes bijections.
plausible_today: Take Omega(V) to be nonzero vectors in the top exterior-power line modulo positive scalars, and define Stokes by adjoining an inward normal last. This satisfies all axioms, including the two-element zero-dimensional value.
state_of_art: ConradOrientations Definitions1.1/1.4 and Examples1.6/1.7 supply the standard determinant-line and exact-sequence orientation model. The full axiom check is given here. Hua2026 p285 explicitly excludes this existence assertion from its verification; it must not be conflated with MP-SA22-404.
why_open: The source reduces the problem to standard-space data but supplies no full model. No historical reason for leaving it open is documented in the sources consulted.
worth: Worth completing in a companion or small formal task; the construction is elementary, while verifying exactly the zero-dimensional and sign conventions is useful.

title: The announced tensor, symmetric and exterior algebra extension

occurrences.quote: Extension aux ... algèbres symétriques, tensorielles, extérieures

as_he_states: Extend the exponential construction to tensor, symmetric and exterior algebras. This is a terse announced task, with no explicit uniform-nilpotence claim.
plausible_today: Extend the generator as a derivation on generators. Formal actions always extend; ordinary actions extend for locally nilpotent generators. If u^r=0, the induced operator on degree d has nilpotence bound d(r−1)+1, with generally no bound independent of d.
state_of_art: Opened Milne2018RG §13.15 checks tensor compatibility; Yuan2017 supplies the local-nilpotence classification of ordinary actions. Passing through the stable symmetric/exterior relations proves the announced extension. The degree bound and Q[x,y] example are checked here; no open residue after making scope explicit.
why_open: The manuscript gives only a heading-like line, then moves to globalization. No reason for postponement is documented.
worth: Worth a short worked example because it makes the uniform/local nilpotence distinction concrete and links scan39 to scan44.

title: The unfinished flag-composition symbol I(omega,omega′)
as_he_states: A flag U⊂W⊂V, a composite of two Stokes maps, and an I(omega,omega′) expression are started, but the target of Omega and the final assertion are missing.
plausible_today: For successive hyperplanes, orient V/U using the exact sequence0→W/U→V/U→V/W→0, in the order W/U then V/W. This is a coherent candidate for the missing datum; it is not recovered text.
state_of_art: ConradOrientations Example1.7 gives the exact-sequence determinant orientation construction. The candidate’s sign and composition are checked here. Neither that source nor Hua2026 §57 identifies the unfinished manuscript symbol; its intended formulation remains F, not an open established conjecture.
why_open: The physical transcription stops at an incomplete target. No source explains whether it was abandoned, continued elsewhere, or merely abbreviated.
worth: Worth a bounded editorial comparison with neighboring orientation sheets; it is low priority as new mathematics because the natural candidate is standard.

title: From a hyperplane stabilizer to the whole general linear group
as_he_states: The source asserts the global sign(det) character after a compatibility equation only on the standard hyperplane stabilizer. This is a proof gap, not a securely marked question.
plausible_today: The full conclusion follows because transvections are squares, reflections act nontrivially by the opposite-half-space axiom, and transvections with invertible diagonal matrices generate GL_n(R).
state_of_art: Exact proof in Hua2026 §57, action statement on p284. It was read and independently checked. No continuity assumption is needed and no unresolved mathematical residue remains.
why_open: The words par récurrence omit the generation step. The source does not mark the final cancelled word securely as Vérifier, and no historical explanation is available.
worth: Worth keeping as a separate dependency in the companion proof, since uniqueness alone does not supply the action classification needed for existence.
